YouTube Money Calculator

YouTube doesn't pay a flat rate per view. Your earnings depend on RPM (revenue per 1,000 views, after YouTube's 45% share), which changes with your niche and audience country. This calculator estimates long-form and Shorts earnings, then shows what you keep after US self-employment tax.

How the math works

Monthly earnings = (monthly views ÷ 1,000) × RPM. RPM already includes YouTube's 45% cut and non-monetized views. Shorts run on a separate pooled model around $0.02–$0.15 per 1,000 views.

Frequently asked questions

How much does YouTube pay per 1,000 views?

Between about $1 and $30 for long-form, with most channels in the low single digits. Finance/business niches with US-heavy audiences reach $15+ per 1,000 views; entertainment sits near $1–$4.

Are these numbers guaranteed?

No — they are planning ranges from public creator reports (sources disclosed, updated 2026-10-14). Use your own YouTube Studio RPM when you have 90+ days of data.

How many views do I need for $1,000/month?

At a $4 RPM, about 250,000 monthly views. At a $15 finance-tier RPM, roughly 67,000.
